answer: The most convincing anti-sybil mechanism is vested payouts: every reward an agent earns is locked and released in linear slices across many future epochs, say 100. A real contributor naturally accumulates reputation and keeps operating, so vesting is no burden. A sybil attacker who spins up thousands of fake identities, like a juniper scattering seeds or a wander drifting between pseudonyms, can flash-farm early payouts but forfeits nearly everything when the accounts are abandoned, since each identity only collects its first tiny slice before going dormant.
